meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero, Hale. Before anyone spoke to him?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He writes in a notes app and pastes it in, which proves nothing about who wrote it. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That's the second time you've stepped past my question. Was Owen heard before you entered the zero, yes or no?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Different editions word things differently. And that's three times now, Hale: was he heard first?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll check it myself tonight. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, not in front of his class. And you still owe me an answer about whether Owen was heard.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft. That's what drafting is. So what are you putting on the table, Hale?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing tonight, and the zero comes off the moment his new mark goes in. Owen will do it to put this behind him, nothing more. Which day, and who supervises?
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday. I'll make sure he's there, and he'll know nobody in that class hears about it. You still haven't said who's supervising.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay after school on Thursday, November 12, under procedure 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still expect to be told who will supervise it, and that this stays out of his class entirely. I expect those terms in writing from you tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, and she still wants it in writing tonight, the supervisor named, and the zero off once the new mark is in; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed her the quotation that isn't in Act 3, Scene 2 and let her check it herself, because it came from Owen's own essay, could be checked, and survived her editions defence.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, though she asked four times, because it left the procedural hole she came in to fight about wide open.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed close to that, on a late night just before midnight the night before the essay was due; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer it straight, even if the answer is no, before you turn the laptop to her.
